title: Mordaunt / Luttrell and others → Ormond, Restoration-year cipher letters in the Carte papers
correspondents: Thomas Luttrell ('Mordauns', to 'M. Robert Burrowes'); unknown; Henry Jermyn → James Butler, Marquess of Ormond
folio_note: 4 letters: f. 632 (2 Mar 1660, nomenclator numbers, infrequent), f. 660 (16 Mar 1660, letters + nomenclator, intermittent), ff. 680-681 (23 Mar 1660, numbers + code words), f. 602 (19 Feb 1661, Jermyn/Montagu mission to France, cipher throughout)
status: EMLO ('Bodleian early modern letter collections', notes by Edward Edwards) describes the cipher system of each but notes no decipherment; the Carte Calendar supplied senders and dates, so it summarises the content. Not in the repo (known.py: Carte 213 no hit). A printed text may exist (27 Oct 2026), but the manuscript is not online, so the print cannot be matched to the cipher yet.
why: Royalist intelligence to Ormond in the weeks before the Restoration and on Jermyn's 1661 French mission.
prior_art: not checked in print (26 Oct 2026); Carte Calendar summaries may reflect a contemporary decipherment; printed text may exist, manuscript not online so it cannot be matched (27 Oct 2026)

title: Thomas Harrison and William Jephson → Henry Cromwell, letters partly in numeric cipher, partly decoded
correspondents: Major-General Thomas Harrison; William Jephson → Henry Cromwell
shelfmark: British Library, Lansdowne MS 821, fols 154-155, 170-171, 290-291, 350-351 (and one more, folio not given)
folio_note: 5 letters; Lansdowne MS 823 ff. 339-340 is a draft code between Henry Cromwell and Lord Broghill (key lead).
status: EMLO (Henry Cromwell catalogue): 'The letter is written in part in a substitutional numeric cipher. It has been transcribed in code ... and attempts at decoding have been made in the footnotes' — i.e. partial decoding only. Not in the repo (known.py: Lansdowne 821 no hit).
why: Jephson was Cromwell's envoy to Charles X of Sweden in 1657; cipher parts carry the diplomatic substance.

title: Comenius → Andreas Klobusiczky, cipher passage of 24 May 1655 (Rákóczi archive)
correspondents: Jan Amos Komenský (Comenius) → Andreas Klobusiczky (Rákóczi's councillor)
shelfmark: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár Országos Levéltár (Budapest), E 190 (Archivum familiae Rákóczi): 5.t. 788 ff. 389-390v; 6962 ff. 351-354v; 5.t. 800 ff. 414-415v
folio_note: One passage of 50 letters and the numbers 7, 865, 73 inside news quoted from an English correspondent; printed MHH XXIII (1874) no. CIII p. 178 and Patera 1892 no. CLII p. 178 (italic). The 4 Aug 1655 sentence is deciphered (write-up comenius1655); 22 Jul and 6 Sept have invisible ink / secret script printed in clear by Szilágyi 1890.
status: 4 Aug 1655 sentence deciphered in print (Szilágyi 1890 p. 393; Patera 1892 p. 182); key = Rákóczi envoys' table, MHH XXIII p. 740. The 24 May passage does not decipher with that table, shifts, keyword ciphers, or as a simple substitution of Latin (annealing with matched control); no decipherment in MHH, Szilágyi 1890 or Patera. See targets/comenius1655/.
why: Comenius's secret line to George II Rákóczi on the Swedish-Polish war of 1655, when he pressed Transylvania to join Sweden.
prior_art: checked 27 Oct 2026: MHH XXIII 1874, Szilágyi 1890 I pp. 388-394, Patera 1892; no decipherment of 24 May

title: Elizabeth Stuart, Queen of Bohemia, correspondence partly in cipher (Roe, Frederick V, Charles Louis, Gerbier)
correspondents: Elizabeth Stuart ↔ Sir Thomas Roe (66); Frederick V (17), Charles I Louis (15), Balthazar Gerbier (17) → Elizabeth
shelfmark: Mainly The National Archives (UK), SP 16 / SP 81 / SP 84 and BL; per-letter shelfmarks on EMLO (catalogue 'Stuart, Elizabeth, Queen of Bohemia')
folio_note: EMLO notes 'This letter is written partly in cipher' on about 115 letters, peaks 1632 (25), 1638 (15), 1639 (25), 1641-42 (24)
status: EMLO notes the cipher but no decipherment; the letters are edited in Nadine Akkerman, The Correspondence of Elizabeth Stuart, Queen of Bohemia (OUP, 3 vols, 2011-2025), whose editor deciphered the Roe and Palatine ciphers. Kept as one row only to record whether any code groups remain unread there. A printed text may exist (27 Oct 2026), but the manuscript is not online, so the print cannot be matched to the cipher yet.
why: Palatine-Stuart diplomacy in the Thirty Years' War; most likely read already.
prior_art: probably deciphered in Akkerman's edition (2011-2025); not checked page by page (26 Oct 2026); printed text may exist, manuscript not online so it cannot be matched (27 Oct 2026)

title: Captain Thomas Ogle and Sir John Digby → Thomas Devenish, code letters (one a code repeat of the other)
correspondents: Thomas Ogle; John Digby, 1st Earl of Bristol → Thomas Devenish
shelfmark: Bodleian Library, MS Tanner 62, fols 498 and 506
folio_note: f. 498 'underlined in code line by line' (reports admission 'on intimation of code numbers'); f. 506 'The preceding letter repeated in code form'
status: Bodleian card catalogue (EMLO). f. 506 is a code version of a letter whose clear text is on f. 498, so the code is a crib pair; no decipherment of other code letters noted. The Ogle-Devenish plot (1643-44) was a Royalist approach to the Independents.
why: Ogle's plot letters; a clear/code pair would give the key to other Ogle plot ciphers in Tanner 62.
prior_art: open as far as checked (26 Oct 2026: EMLO, known.py); the plot is printed in Gardiner, not checked for the code

title: John Graham → James Madison, Burr conspiracy reports in State Department code, partly read
correspondents: John Graham (State Department agent sent after Burr) → James Madison
shelfmark: Library of Congress, Burr Conspiracy Collection (DLC)
folio_note: 2 documents: RC 12 Nov 1806 (Madison/02-13-02-0044) and undated extract [22 Nov 1806] (Madison/02-13-02-0081); the extract prints several numerals for which 'there is as yet no key' (46, 73, 71, 18 ...)
status: Editors: 'encoded by Graham using a State Department code, decoded here by the editors with assistance from James E. Lewis's partially reconstructed key. The numerals in the text represent words for which there is as yet no key.' Partly decoded interlinearly by Wagner on the 12 Nov letter. Not in the repo (known.py: Graham, Burr no hit). Attempted 26 Oct 2026 (targets/graham1806/): Pinckney legation code and Armstrong's THE=972 code ruled out on the open groups; the likely code is the State Department code printed in Weber 1979 pp. 419-30 (used for Graham's 2 Jan 1806 letter, Founders 02-11-02-0004), not obtained; LoC Burr Conspiracy Collection not digitised (microfilm 17,112).
why: Graham's reports were the government's first inside intelligence on Burr and Blennerhassett; the unread groups are names and places.
prior_art: read in part by the Madison Papers editors with J. E. Lewis's partial key (checked 26 Oct 2026)
